Fix: Tighten these words to the reference pace; keep length only on the stressed word.

regions.explanation: From 22.72s to 30.00s (“prosperity and the still waters of peace. Yet, every so …”), 4 pause(s) at punctuation shrank from 363 ms to 0 ms on average. Pauses at punctuation mark the end of an idea and give the audience time to absorb it; running through them merges separate thoughts into one stream. Fix: Hold a clear pause at each punctuation mark, about as long as the reference.

From 25.94s to 26.86s (“every so often the”), articulation rate was 7.61 syll/s against 4.17 syll/s in the reference (+83%); that is 1.5× the reference speaker's natural word-to-word variation. Faster articulation compresses the stressed syllables and the micro-pauses listeners use to segment phrases, so key words lose emphasis and comprehension drops. Fix: Slow to the reference pace here and let the pauses between clauses breathe.
